# Changelog {#changelog .unnumbered}

This book is a living document. Major additions and changes are recorded here so returning readers can see what is new. It is developed openly on [GitHub](https://github.com/pem725/GradStats-Book), where the full commit history lives in detail; this page is the readable summary.

## 2026

### New parts and chapters

- **Preparing Our Data** part added - the [Data Reduction](31-datareduction.qmd) chapter (fewer, better measures; reliability to power).
- **Latent Variable Models** part added - [CFA/SEM](28-sem.qmd), [Measurement Invariance](32-invariance.qmd), [Latent Class](29-latentclass.qmd), and [IRT & Generalizability](30-irt.qmd).
- **Causal Inference** part added - [DAGs and the back-door criterion](33-causal.qmd), from the *Statistical Rethinking* course.
- **Beyond the Normal Curve** part added - resampling, robust methods, and Bayesian inference.
- **Displaying Data** part added - [Graphics](21-graphics.qmd) and [Tables](22-tables.qmd).
- **Statistics in the Wild** apprenticeship part added - [The Sports Page](23-sportspage.qmd) and four case studies (depression profiles, building a measure, missing data).
- **The Methods in Practice** [showcase](27-methods-showcase.qmd) added - the authors' published work, organized by method.
- The [Coding Categorical Predictors](19-coding.qmd) chapter and the [Rasch](18-rasch.qmd) chapter (honoring Ben Wright, using his Knox Cube Test data).

### Enrichments to existing chapters

- Anscombe's quartet and the residual bridge added to the [covariance chapter](07-covariance.qmd).
- Types of sums of squares (variance partitioning) added to [multiple regression](15-MRC.qmd).
- Measurement models (parallel, tau-equivalent, congeneric), a generalizability-theory framing, and "Variance Is the Fuel" (restriction of range) added to the [reliability chapter](10-reliability.qmd).
- POMP scoring added to the [z-distribution chapter](06-zdistribution.qmd).
- The replication-crisis Bayes calculation and estimation-versus-testing asides woven through the inference chapters.

### The code itself

- **Every running example rewritten in the tidyverse.** `dplyr` and `tibble` in place of `data.frame` and `$`-indexing, `ggplot2` in place of the last base plots, `purrr::map_*` in place of `sapply`/`replicate`/`apply`, `readr` in place of `read.csv`, and `broom` for printing model results. The statistical engines (`lm`, `aov`, `glm`, `factanal`, `prcomp`) are still base R, and so is every from-scratch derivation.
- **Two decimal places everywhere**, via a shared `round2()` helper, so results are readable and consistent. P-values are the deliberate exception: three decimals, with anything below .001 reported as `< .001`, because a p-value rounded to `0.00` reads as a certainty no p-value ever has.
- A [setup page](required-packages.qmd) documenting the packages and reprinting the three shared helpers in full.

### Presentation and back matter

- Light and dark reading modes with a navbar toggle (defaulting to light), framed figure cards, tidy tables, and larger key-term callouts with a 🔑 marker.
- A voice pass across the whole book for clear, supportive prose.
- Inviting cover, author biographies, and a to-be-written foreword.
- This back matter added: the [changelog](changelog.qmd), the [required-packages](required-packages.qmd) setup page, and the [R / SPSS / Julia / Python](three-languages.qmd) code-tabs appendix.

## Origins

The book began as a set of chapter drafts and an introduction, and grew into a full graduate methods text drawn from the authors' decades of teaching and research in the social and behavioral sciences.
